Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Rajeev Upadhyay, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri G.P. Singh, learned A.G.A.
for the State-respondent nos.1 to 3.
Sri Rahul Singh Tomar, Advocate has filed his Vakalatnama on behalf of respondent no.4/informant, which is taken on record.

2. Present writ petition has been preferred for quashing the FIR dated 06.1.2024 registered as Case Crime No. 02 of 2024, under sections 498A, 313, 376, 511, 504, 506, 323, 307, 406 I.P.C. and section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District-Meerut. and for a direction to Samsher Singh And 6 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191083300/
1 respondents not to arrest the petitioners pursuant to aforesaid FIR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. At the very outset, learned A.G.A. on the instructions, submitted that in the aforesaid case crime,
chargesheet has already been submitted before the competent court, hence, the writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not maintainable.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the impugned first information report has been lodged by respondent no. 4, who is the wife of petitioner no. 3, roping in the entire family of her husband with the ulterior intention of harassing them.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the present matter relates to matrimonial dispute between the parties, which can be resolved before the Mediation Centre of this Court.

It is further contended that there is ample chance of reconciliation between the husband and the wife,
therefore, the matter may be referred to the Mediation Centre.
Learned counsel for respondent no.4/informant has given a nod to the aforesaid submissions.

6. In view of the above, it is directed that petitioners shall deposit a sum of Rs.35,000/- within 15 days from today with the Mediation Centre of this Court, out of which Rs.30,000/- shall be paid to respondent no.4, on the date fixed, for her appearance before the Mediation Centre and Rs.5000/-
shall be retained by the Mediation Centre as mediation fee.
7.

The matter is remitted to the Mediation Centre with the direction that after deposit of aforesaid amount, by the petitioners, it shall issue notice to the parties fixing some date for mediation and shall make all possible efforts to conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously,
preferably within a period of three months.

8. List after expiry of aforesaid period before the appropriate Bench along with the report of Mediation Centre.
9.
Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners in the above mentioned case.

10. It is made clear that in case petitioners default in either depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed, the interim order shall cease to operate and the Mediation Centre shall immediately communicate with the office which in turn shall list the case within a week before the appropriate Bench for passing orders in the matter.

Order Date :- 4.12.2024 Faridul  Samsher Singh And 6 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191083300/
